concepts.name: Multiplication history and the n log n conjecture
concepts.gloss: Schönhage–Strassen gave O(n log n log log n) and conjectured n log n optimal; Fürer and others improved the factor; Harvey–van der Hoeven reached O(n log n).

evidence.quote: proposed $n\log n$ as the optimal order of growth

concepts.name: Multiplication as convolution of radix digits
concepts.gloss: Splitting both integers into short radix digits turns the integer product into a convolution of digit lists, followed by carry propagation.

evidence.quote: Splitting the inputs into radix digits reduces multiplication to
convolution of short integer coefficients

concepts.name: Fourier transforms and butterfly operations
concepts.gloss: A discrete Fourier transform evaluates a sequence at roots of unity, turning cyclic convolution into pointwise products; fast versions use layers of two-point butterflies.

evidence.quote: the transform calculation consists of address
rearrangements, signed shifts, and two-point butterfly operations

concepts.gloss: Harvey–van der Hoeven reduction expressing a Fourier transform of arbitrary axis length through a transform with power-of-two axes, with source and target permutations kept in the identity.

concepts.name: Phase twist to the polynomial ring
concepts.gloss: A twist on the last cyclic coordinate makes its wraparound negative, turning it into a polynomial modulo y^r+1 whose negative wrap restores the cyclic wrap after untwisting.

evidence.quote: A phase twist changes the last cyclic coordinate into a polynomial

concepts.name: Binary representation and radix digits
concepts.gloss: A nonnegative integer is written as a string of digits in a given base, with the leftmost digit most significant.

concepts.name: Modular arithmetic and congruences
concepts.gloss: Integers are compared by their remainders on division by a modulus, and arithmetic is done on these remainders.

concepts.name: Prime numbers and coprimality
concepts.gloss: A prime has no divisors besides 1 and itself, and integers with gcd 1 are coprime.

concepts.name: Logarithms and powers of two
concepts.gloss: lg n is the base-2 logarithm, and ceiling and floor round up and down to integers.

concepts.name: Schoolbook multiplication and convolution of sequences
concepts.gloss: The product of two polynomials has coefficients given by sums of products of pairs of coefficients with indices adding to the given degree.

concepts.name: Karatsuba and divide-and-conquer multiplication
concepts.gloss: Recursively splitting operands into halves to multiply faster than the quadratic schoolbook method.

concepts.name: Fast Fourier transform basics
concepts.gloss: The standard O(N log N) algorithm for evaluating a sequence at the N-th roots of unity, using the primitive complex root of unity e^{2 pi i/N}.

concepts.name: Linear algebra over the reals and complex numbers
concepts.gloss: Vectors, matrices, linear maps, invertibility, subspaces and dimension.

concepts.name: Direct product of sets and multidimensional arrays
concepts.gloss: A multidimensional array is indexed by tuples of coordinates, one per axis, and stored linearly in some order.

concepts.name: Permutations and bijections
concepts.gloss: A permutation is a bijective rearrangement of positions, which can be composed and inverted.

concepts.name: Cyclic groups and Z/mZ
concepts.gloss: Integers modulo m under addition, with indices wrapping around.

concepts.name: Fixed-point and rounding arithmetic
concepts.gloss: Numbers represented with a fixed number of bits after the point, with rounding errors bounded and tracked.

concepts.name: Error bounds and the triangle inequality
concepts.gloss: Magnitudes of sums are bounded by sums of magnitudes, and the maximum absolute value of coordinates measures a vector.

concepts.name: Binary XOR and bitwise operations
concepts.gloss: Bitwise operations on binary words, with XOR being addition mod 2 on each bit.

concepts.name: Basic counting and combinatorics
concepts.gloss: Counting subsets and intersections of finite sets.

concepts.name: Induction and recurrences
concepts.gloss: Proving statements recursively and solving recurrences for running time.

concepts.name: Real analysis basics: inequalities and exponentials
concepts.gloss: Standard facts about exp, sine, cosine, and bounding sums by integrals.

concepts.name: Ring and group axioms
concepts.gloss: Sets with addition and multiplication satisfying standard laws, as met in discrete mathematics.

background.summary: An undergraduate computer science reader who has studied discrete mathematics, algorithms (divide and conquer, fast multiplication such as Karatsuba, the FFT at a basic level), linear algebra, and elementary number theory and probability. They know asymptotic notation, binary and positional number representation, polynomials and complex numbers, and basic Turing machines. They have not studied multitape complexity details, advanced harmonic analysis, algebraic number theory, or the research literature on integer multiplication.
